catalysts.title: Hyperscaler AI Data Center Power Interconnection Demand Supercycle
catalysts.probabilityAnchor: Electrification segment orders rose 66% organically in Q2 2026, with data center-related orders exceeding $5.0B year-to-date, more than doubling total FY2025 volumes.
catalysts.description: Generative AI training and inference clusters demand gigawatts of firm, non-intermittent electrical capacity. Tier-1 hyperscalers (Microsoft, AWS, Google, Meta) are contracting directly for on-site aeroderivative gas turbines, HA-class combined cycle units, and custom substation interconnections to bypass 5-7 year public utility grid connection backlogs.

evidence.fact: GE Vernova booked over $5.0B of AI data center equipment orders in the first six months of 2026, with multi-gigawatt behind-the-meter turbine deals in active procurement.

catalysts.title: Heavy-Duty Gas Turbine Delivery Slot Scarcity Through 2029
catalysts.probabilityAnchor: Power equipment backlog and slot reservations reached 116 GW in Q2 2026, with management projecting >=125 GW by year-end, effectively selling out factory production slots through 2029.
catalysts.description: Global utilities and independent power producers face acute baseload capacity shortages driven by data centers, industrial onshoring, and coal retirements. This has created unprecedented delivery slot scarcity for GE Vernova's HA and F-class gas turbines, enabling double-digit price increases, non-refundable slot reservation fees, and high-margin multi-decade Contractual Service Agreements (CSAs).

evidence.fact: Power segment orders jumped 134% organically to $16.7B in Q2 2026, with gas equipment backlog and slot reservations expanding to 116 GW.

catalysts.title: Electrification Grid Solutions Operating Margin Expansion
catalysts.probabilityAnchor: Electrification revenue surged 68% YoY to $3.6B, with EBITDA margin reaching 13.3% as pre-inflation legacy fixed-price backlog burns off and high-margin grid solutions scale.
catalysts.description: Grid Solutions, High-Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) transmission links, and GIS switchgear are experiencing structural operating leverage. With the legacy fixed-price backlog largely executed, new deliveries priced at current peak levels will drive segment margins toward 16-18% over FY2027.

evidence.fact: Electrification segment EBITDA margin expanded by 340 bps YoY to 13.3%, while segment orders reached $6.3B (+66% organic).

source.title: GE Vernova Q2 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

catalysts.title: Onshore Wind Operating Margin Recovery and Repowering Wave
catalysts.probabilityAnchor: Onshore wind order margins have turned solidly positive following SKU rationalization to workhorse turbine platforms and surging US repowering demand.
catalysts.description: After rationalizing turbine variants down to proven 3.6MW and 6.1MW platforms and exiting unprofitable geographical markets, Onshore Wind is poised to inflect to mid-to-high single-digit operating margins by FY2027, propelled by US turbine repowering cycles under IRA PTC tax credits.

evidence.fact: Management indicated that newly contracted onshore wind projects carry high single-digit operating margins, contrasting sharply with legacy offshore contracts.

catalysts.title: Offshore Wind Legacy Contract Losses and Blade Warranty Tail-Risk
catalysts.probabilityAnchor: Wind segment incurred a -$275M EBITDA loss in Q2 2026, accompanied by an ongoing federal investigation into the Vineyard Wind blade failure and court injunction blocking contract termination.
catalysts.description: Manufacturing defects identified in Haliade-X offshore turbine blades (insufficient adhesive bonding) and remaining legacy offshore wind backlog execution subject GEV to persistent warranty remediation costs, installation delay liquidated damages, and specialized marine vessel charter penalties.

evidence.fact: GE Vernova recorded $320M in incremental warranty and remediation provisions in Q2 2026, while a Massachusetts court granted a preliminary injunction preventing contract cancellation with Vineyard Wind.

source.title: GE Vernova Form 10-Q Part I Item 1

catalysts.title: Utility Transformer Supply Chain Lead Times and Component Bottlenecks
catalysts.probabilityAnchor: Lead times for large high-voltage power transformers extend beyond 3 to 4 years globally due to severe shortages in grain-oriented electrical steel (GOES) and skilled winding labor.
catalysts.description: While extended lead times provide visibility, acute shortages of electrical grade steel, copper conductors, and high-voltage bushings could cap electrification delivery throughput and push revenue recognition past FY2027.

evidence.fact: Industry lead times for utility substations and power transformers remain at 150-210 weeks, prompting GE Vernova to commit dedicated capital investments to expand transformer manufacturing lines in North America and Europe.
